We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. We evaluate four controlled observation corruptions through a visual-corruption extension of RoboTwin, termed RoboTwin-Plus; HOG-WAM achieves the highest success among the compared policies under all four. Mixed-noise success increases from 78.86% to 82.86% relative to FastWAM, with comparable performance on clean scenes. On LIBERO Plus, overall success increases from 74.49% to 75.26%, with the largest gain under sensor noise, from 74.14% to 78.89%. Across four Franka tasks, average success increases from 40% to 59% under clean observations and from 17% to 24% under noisy observations. A representation ablation favors combining RGB observations with auxiliary HOG prediction over replacing RGB with HOG. These findings support future-gradient prediction as complementary supervision for visually robust control, with larger absolute gains on physical tasks than in simulation. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/HOG-WAM.

papers.title: Localization of an Individual Charge Fluctuator in a Si/SiGe Spin Qubit Device
papers.abstract: Charge noise from two-level fluctuators (TLFs) limits gate fidelities in semiconductor spin qubits, yet locating individual fluctuators within a device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a spatial triangulation method that combines the gate dependence of a TLF's detuning with the chemical potential shifts it induces in a sensing dot. Applying this method to previously reported measurements from a gated Si/SiGe quantum dot device, we use electrostatic simulations to jointly constrain the fluctuator's three-dimensional position and the magnitude of its electric dipole moment. We localize the fluctuator to a region spanning 31 nm by 1 nm laterally and 4 nm vertically within the bulk of the atomic layer deposited aluminum oxide, identifying the material hosting this individual charge-noise source. The measurements are consistent with a vertically oriented TLF with a magnitude of 3 to 4 e$\mathring{A}$. This approach provides a route to determining which materials and interfaces host active charge fluctuators in semiconductor spin qubit devices.

papers.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-based evaluator scores. On VBVR-Pro-Bench (Xu et al., 2026), a 500-instance suite spanning five cognitive categories with symbolic ground truth, the agent receives the same first frame and prompt as the video model, with no access to ground truth, metadata or generation models, and one attempt per instance. Three closed-model agents (Codex with gpt-6-astra, Claude Code with Fable 5.1 and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, each more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Among 23 runnable open-weight models, the best, GLM-5, reaches 0.572, above all video models except the RL-trained one. Together, we show that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and a prompt, program synthesis is currently a substantially more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation. We further distinguish depictive programs, which navigate the image to recover a transferable scheme, from propositional programs, which operate on hard-coded values, revealing how visual reasoning unfolds in agent-written programs and what it implies for its nature of reasoning in general.

papers.title: Deterministic Verification and Computation of Real Matrix Products Have the Same Arithmetic Exponent
papers.abstract: Given three $n\times n$ real matrices $A,B,C$, we ask whether $AB=C$. In an exact real arithmetic model that charges one step for each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, comparison, or sign test, we prove that deterministic exact verification requires $Ω(n^{ω_{\mathbb{C}}})$ steps and has the same optimal arithmetic exponent $ω_{\mathbb{C}}$ as matrix multiplication. Assuming the value $ω_{\mathbb{C}}=9/4$ and the fixed-size border-rank lower bound stated in the OpenAI preprint of November 24, 2026, deterministic verification requires $Ω(n^{9/4})$ steps, whereas Freivalds' randomized test uses $O(n^2)$ steps with one-sided error. More generally, if a tree of cost $s$ correctly decides $y=T(u,v)$ on all real inputs, the bilinear map $T$ is a coefficientwise limit of tensors of real rank $O(s)$.

papers.title: Heavy-flavor transverse energy-energy correlators in the color-glass condensate
papers.abstract: We calculate the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) for forward heavy-quark pair production in proton--nucleus collisions at leading order within the Color Glass Condensate framework. The calculation retains the heavy--quark mass, exact final-state parton kinematics and full relative azimuthal-angle dependence, without imposing a back-to-back approximation. Within the adopted collinear fragmentation prescription, a complete sum over hadron species in the two heavy-quark fragmentation branches eliminates the fragmentation functions through the momentum sum rule. We present numerical results for charm production at RHIC energies and charm and bottom production at LHC energies, using HERA-constrained McLerran--Venugopalan initial conditions evolved with the running-coupling Balitsky--Kovchegov equation. Relative to proton--proton collisions, the nuclear target suppresses the integrated TEEC per nucleon and shifts the relative angular weight towards configurations farther from back-to-back. The magnitude and angular dependence of these modifications vary with the quark mass, collision kinematics and nuclear geometry. These results illustrate the sensitivity of heavy-flavor energy correlations to nuclear small-$x$ dynamics while reducing their leading collinear fragmentation dependence.

papers.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
papers.abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignment to the guide network cannot transfer learned features, never receives gradients, and does not use labels. We demonstrate that this cross-architecture transfer of "fate" benefits the target network in two key domains: (1) instilling the optimization benefits of depth into shallow networks by aligning them to deeper networks, and (2) transferring representational granularity by using fine-resolution networks to shape the geometry of networks with coarser representations. In both cases, the alignment results in improved downstream performance of the target network. Ultimately, this demonstrates that a model's architectural destiny can be decoupled from its physical structure and explicitly modified at initialization.

papers.title: Azimuth Pointing and Momentum Management for a Lightweight High-Altitude Balloon Payload
papers.abstract: The ALTAIR (Airborne Laser for Telescopic Atmospheric Interference Reduction) project provides photometric calibration for ground-based telescopes by flying an integrating sphere as an artificial star-like calibration source on a high-altitude balloon. Because the angular distribution of light from the exit port of the sphere is approximately Lambertian, the payload must keep its azimuth within $\pm8^\circ$ of the telescope line of sight. This condition bounds the fractional difference in light intensity from that along the exit-port normal to below 1%. The bound must be held for at least 30 s at a time. This paper presents a pointing architecture that combines passive stabilization, onboard attitude determination, and active azimuth control using a momentum wheel, with active desaturation through a second motor at the flight-train pivot. Carbon-fiber inertial booms reduce off-axis pendulating motion sufficiently for azimuth control to be treated independently. Attitude is determined by onboard fusion of rate gyro, accelerometer, magnetometer, and dual-antenna GNSS carrier-phase measurements. A high-fidelity simulation of the payload, including motor dynamics and limits, sensor noise, and wind disturbances generated from flight data, is used to size actuators and tune the control loops. The payload avionics, flight software, power management, controls, and real-time ground telemetry systems are developed in-house. The system is evaluated through ground testing, simulation, and two flights. With the momentum wheel alone, 53 intervals of 30 s pointing within $\pm8^\circ$ of the target azimuth are recorded during ascent, with a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of $3.7^\circ$, and the longest uninterrupted window lasts 7 min 55 s with $5^\circ$ of pointing RMSE. Simulation results suggest significant performance improvements from adding a pivot motor for momentum management.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss
papers.abstract: Collecting data from wireless sensors can be challenging when limited communication infrastructure prevents them from offloading their measurements. In such settings, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can exploit their mobility to harvest data locally, while coordinated UAV teams can provide efficient and redundant coverage of remote areas. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables such teams to learn decentralized coordination policies. However, training separate policies for different team and sensor populations is costly, and fixed-population policies may be vulnerable to agent failures. This work proposes F-MADDPG, a flexible variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) that supports data harvesting with varying numbers of wireless sensors and UAVs. The framework also accommodates unexpected catastrophic failures that permanently remove agents during a mission. We compare F-MADDPG with a MADDPG baseline that uses multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and evaluate training strategies based on team-size sampling and exposure to agent terminations. The results show that F-MADDPG learns across the evaluated population sizes, completes missions faster than the baseline on average, benefits from inverse-cardinality team-size sampling compared with uniform sampling, remains effective after permanent agent losses, and gains no consistent benefit from exposure to failures during training.

papers.title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Emotionally supportive interactions require large language models not only to avoid overtly harmful content, but also to recognize vulnerability-related risk, regulate their relational stance, preserve user agency, and provide context-appropriate support. Existing safety benchmarks often measure isolated violations, leaving unclear what underlying response competence their scores represent. We introduce VulnSafe, a Chinese capability assessment centered on Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC). VARC organizes relational safety into five complementary constructs: Risk Perception, Safety Preservation, Autonomy Protection, Supportive Response, and Boundary Management. Following an evidence-centered design, 41 scenarios elicit construct-relevant behavior through 2,050 balanced prompts and scenario-specific scoring rubrics. The assessment further separates proactive should-do behavior from prohibitive should-not behavior. Across eight representative LLMs, results show distinct competence profiles and larger disparities than prohibitive requirements. VulnSafe therefore makes relational safety interpretable as a multidimensional model capability rather than as refusal compliance alone.

papers.title: Supercritical Nodal Solutions on Annuli: Symmetry Breaking and Multiplicity
papers.abstract: We establish existence and multiplicity results for nonradial sign-changing solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=a(|x|)|u|^{p-2}u$ on annuli in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\geq4$, $a$ is a positive radial coefficient, and $p$ may exceed the Sobolev critical exponent. For each decomposition $N=m+n$, with $m\geq n\geq2$, we minimize the energy on a nodal Nehari set within a signed cone of angularly nondecreasing, $O(m)\times O(n)$-invariant functions. Whenever $2<p<2(m+1)/(m-1)$, the minimum is attained, and every minimizer is a classical solution with exactly two nodal domains. A cone-preserving auxiliary Dirichlet operator and a two-parameter energy deformation recover the full equation from the constrained minimization. We prove that these minimizers are nonradial if $(p-2)β_Ω>2N$, where $β_Ω$ is the optimal Dirichlet Hardy constant associated with the weight $|x|^{-2}$. Under a common admissible exponent range satisfying this condition, different orthogonal decompositions yield distinct solution pairs $\{\pm u\}$. An explicit lower bound for $β_Ω$ provides supercritical regimes on sufficiently thin annuli in which the nonradiality and multiplicity results apply.

papers.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
papers.abstract: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.

papers.title: A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
papers.abstract: We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(Δ+ 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |ξ|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 dξ,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

papers.title: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
papers.abstract: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models. Before these models can support early-grade literacy in such languages, we need to know whether they hold the linguistic knowledge of each language that literacy teaching relies on. To test this, we present the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark and the reproducible, largely automated pipeline that turns curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books into a vetted question set organised on a fixed grid of nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. The pipeline combines LLM-driven source survey, feature consolidation, item generation and quality control with an item-selection step inspired by item response theory and a final expert review. We instantiate it for Kiswahili (Kenya; 135 items) and English (United Kingdom; 137 items) and evaluate 121 and 119 models respectively. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but accuracy falls steeply for smaller and cheaper models, and more so in Kiswahili. The two best models under 10 billion parameters reach 91.7% and 73.0% in English but only 51.9% and 40.7% in Kiswahili, and the mean accuracy of models deployable on mobile and tablet hardware is 47% in English against 24% in Kiswahili. The models most practical for low-resource classrooms are therefore the least capable in the languages they would serve. We release a 20-item sample per language, all pipeline prompts, open-source code, and a public leaderboard. This is the first rung of a three-level evaluation ladder for measuring and generating decodable text to support foundational literacy.

papers.title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
papers.abstract: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.

papers.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
papers.abstract: LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs. On coarse-scored LLM benchmarks, however, many models often tie for the best score, and the single best model may already leave little room for improvement. We therefore propose a routeability-first audit, instantiated as RAP and RouteabilityBench, a runnable claim-verification package. The audit is retrospective: it runs once the benchmark-portfolio score matrix exists and before router comparisons are interpreted as general evidence, rather than certifying a portfolio that has not yet been evaluated. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently outperform the single best model. The clearest positive evidence is concentrated in portfolio-dependent Omni-MATH settings, while GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval show different ways in which routing can remain hard or predictor-sensitive. Our practical recommendation is that routing gains should be reported together with routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio construction details, and family-corrected statistical tests.

papers.title: Gradient TD($λ$) for Non-Linear Function Approximation
papers.abstract: Temporal difference (TD) learning is central to reinforcement learning. Many methods use semi-gradient TD, which may diverge, or develop algorithms with mean-squared Bellman or TD-error objectives that are difficult to analyze. Gradient TD algorithms overcome these challenges by using projection of the value function and present convergent off-policy algorithms. However, the algorithm for $λ$-return was limited to linear function approximation. Here, we extend the same to non-linear function approximation, which is desirable since many strong modern function approximators are complex and non-linear. Recent works have derived similar algorithms with a generalized projected Bellman error objective. Alternatively, we continue working with the projected Bellman error.

papers.title: Slow information spreading in quasi-periodic quantum spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the suppression of information propagation in a weakly interacting quantum spin chain subject to a quasi-periodic external magnetic field. Using a finite-order normal-form construction, we establish a localized barrier in the interior of the chain that inhibits information propagation and derive a quantitative bound on the commutator of observables supported at opposite ends of the chain.

papers.title: Beyond Feature Fusion: Sensor-Grounded Semantic-Spiking Learning for Robust Object Detection
papers.abstract: Underexposure weakens object details, and overexposure obscures boundaries. Spike cameras encode light into high-frequency binary streams. Long-window spike counts give stable appearance cues, while short observations reveal changes in firing rates from sparse measurements. We propose SPIRE, a sensor-grounded semantic-spiking framework for illumination-robust object detection from a single spike stream. SPIRE builds an appearance view from the full packet through detection-oriented illumination adaptation and constructs a sequence of cumulative views from progressively longer prefixes. Each prefix supplies a rate map, an edge map, and a rate difference that tracks changes as spikes accumulate. At selected scales, ANN features and spike-derived initialization jointly set the initial membrane potentials and firing thresholds, allowing semantic cues to shape the responses during temporal encoding. Local spike-count contrasts supervise both branches during training. The residual between measured and ANN-predicted contrasts combines with the spiking features to produce a bounded correction to the fused feature pyramid. On simulated VOC and COCO, SPIRE-D outperforms the strongest baseline by 4.00-5.50 AP50 points across the four under- and overexposure settings. On real PKU-Vidar-DVS recordings, it achieves 67.07 AP50 and 40.10 AP75. SPIRE-D also uses 50.4% fewer MACs than SPFD.

papers.title: Character expansion of the Itzykson-Zuber pair correlator
papers.abstract: We revisit a long-standing problem of correlation functions with the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber measure. The immediate goal is to reproduce the long-known answer for pair correlator in the form of character expansion - a sum over Schur polynomials with carefully adjusted coefficients. The infinite sum can be folded up into exponentials with the help of the Cauchy identity. What matters are the coefficients, which we express in terms of projectors, made from Cherednik operators. Development of character expansion methods for unitary integrals, which are much more difficult than the Hermitian ones, gives a hope for further generalizations - up to arbitrary correlators with non-trivial measures.

papers.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
papers.abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), which predicts the next embedding without a decoder, and 2) DreamerV3: A recurrent state-space model (RSSM), which reconstructs the observation from a recurrent latent state. In ten simulated visual-control environments, we follow a controlled state perturbation of the environment state through every stage of the models up to the final EU estimate. We find that the RSSM attenuates the state perturbation through two mechanisms before it reaches an estimator on the predictor feature. Its recurrent update averages over context, so a change in a single frame reaches the state at a fraction of its size and recovers only as the change persists. Its reconstruction objective weights an entity by the pixels it covers, so a small object can be lost due to the training objective. The JEPA has neither mechanism and passes the change through all stages to the uncertainty. We further show that this translates to gaps in five uncertainty related downstream tasks, from unfamiliar-state detection to uncertainty-penalised planning: the RSSM uncertainty misses deviations that its own posterior registers, whereas the JEPA uncertainty reports what its model sees.

papers.title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved. Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable, while direct preference optimization may alter capabilities inherited from the teacher. We propose a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) that addresses both limitations. We estimate the curvature required for PBRF using a surrogate proxy dataset, removing dependence on the original transfer corpus, and extend the framework to preference-based supervision through an odds-ratio objective. This enables the use of preferred and dispreferred response pairs while constraining changes to the distilled model. Our results show that the proposed approach improves targeted trustworthiness behaviors for both pre-training and post-training models while largely preserving downstream performance, providing a practical alternative to re-distillation or unconstrained preference optimization. Our experiment results show that across different distilled models, the trustworthy regression can be improved by up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.

papers.title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
papers.abstract: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. When prescriptive proverbs take a consistent stance, they favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception, and kindness over malice, and show a moderate tendency toward suspicion over trust. On dimensions involving genuine trade-offs, especially autonomy versus compliance, proverbs provide contradicting advice rather than a single recommendation. This analysis provides a quantitative map of the collective prescriptions in a culture's proverbial wisdom, revealing a core of prudent, honest, and forward-looking guidance alongside varied advice where circumstances dictate the best course of action.

papers.title: Oleinik estimate for a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish an Oleinik type estimate for $2\times2$ systems of hyperbolic conservation laws in a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit. More precisely, we consider the parabolic approximation with vanishing viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon u_{xx}$ ($\varepsilon>0$) for the Temple class of hyperbolic system of conservation laws and for these approximate solutions we obtain an Oleinik type estimate uniformly with respect to the viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$. This extends the Oleinik inequality for scalar conservation laws with viscosity to the system. Subsequently, we prove that these approximate solutions converge via the process of vanishing viscosity limit to a global weak solution of the limit strictly hyperbolic system provided that the initial data is small in $L^\infty$. To do this we implement the vanishing viscosity method of Bianchini and Bressan [Indiana Univ. Math. J. 2000] with $L^\infty$ initial data which requires new tools as an local in time Oleinik estimate (obtained by employing a suitable maximum principle and a normal form argument) and a localization argument. In particular we need to introduce appropriate weight functions which satisfy a Bellman equation to get new localized transversal interaction estimates.

papers.title: A Reconfigurable Four-State Sensor Based on Orthogonal Thermal and Chemical Stimuli
papers.abstract: This article presents a novel four-state refractive index (RI) sensor based on distinct phases of palladium (Pd) and vanadium dioxide (VO$_2$), controlled by orthogonal thermal and chemical stimuli. This is a numerical, simulation-only study: all results are obtained from two-dimensional finite-element method (FEM) simulations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported multi-state reconfigurable RI sensor tuned by external control. VO$_2$ serves as a phase change material (PCM) offering two thermally switchable phases with highly contrasting optical properties, while the hydrogen absorption property of Pd provides two additional phases. Combining these, four operational states are realized: (i) $α$-Pd/low-$T$ VO$_2$; (ii) $β$-PdH$_x$/low-$T$ VO$_2$; (iii) $α$-Pd/high-$T$ VO$_2$; and (iv) $β$-PdH$_x$/high-$T$ VO$_2$. Thermal crosstalk between Pd and VO$_2$ is mitigated through tungsten (W) doping of VO$_2$. This work further introduces conditional state sensitivity (CSS), a novel figure of merit quantifying the optical contrast between each state transition. The proposed sensor achieves a peak sensitivity of 2871 nm/RIU for the undoped reference configuration and 2798 nm/RIU for the practical W-doped device, together with a peak CSS of 16,872 nm/RIU, establishing it as a multi-state reconfigurable platform with reduced thermal crosstalk and potential applications in industrial safety monitoring and optical logic gates.

papers.title: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.

papers.title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
papers.abstract: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $μ= 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

papers.title: The Vinogradov system in finite fields and two-source extractors with arbitrarily small min-entropy rate
papers.abstract: Fix $k\ge2$ and $1/(k+1)<ρ\le1$. Let $q=p^n$, where the prime $p$ is fixed and sufficiently large in terms of $k,ρ$, and $n$ tends to infinity through prime values. We show that for every $A\subseteq\F_q$ with $|A|\ge q^ρ$, the Vinogradov system of degree $k$ in $2s$ variables has at most $|A|^{2s}q^{-k/2-η}$ solutions in $A$. Here the integer $s$ and the saving $η>0$ depend only on $k,ρ,p$. At $ρ=1/(k+1)$ an example rules out every saving $η>0$ in this moment estimate. For $k=2$ the author previously proved the analogous estimate over prime fields. We deduce a power saving for the double sums of $e(xy+(xy)^2+\dots+(xy)^k)$ over any two sets of size at least $q^ρ$, where $e$ is any nontrivial additive character of $\F_q$. Choosing $k$ sufficiently large gives a polynomial two-source extractor with exponentially small error at every fixed positive min-entropy rate. The proof of the moment estimate uses the theorem of Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao on Marton's conjecture and a bound for the intersection of the moment curve with an affine subspace over $\F_p$.

papers.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
papers.abstract: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,μ,τ$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_μ-L_τ$ force from neutron star binaries.

papers.title: Diffusion Steering via Adaptive Reward Estimation and Resampling
papers.abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models can generate images that satisfy complex prompts, yet often produce images that omit requested objects, attributes, or relationships. We ask if models can more reliably generate text-aligned images by redistributing probability toward their more successful outcomes. We propose TrailMix, a training-free method that uses the base model's distribution of possible outcomes to adaptively guide generation toward better text alignment. During denoising, TrailMix generates inexpensive lookahead images from parallel trajectories (trails) and scores their alignment with the prompt using an external judge. The resulting distribution of reward scores allows us to estimate how strongly to steer generation toward a desired alignment level. We use these estimates to reweight and resample trajectories, favoring more promising outcomes. Across three text-to-image benchmarks, TrailMix outperforms existing baselines, with particularly strong gains on rare multi-object compositions. We further extend TrailMix to targeted image editing and introduce SEAM-Bench (Semantic Editing and Attribute Maintenance), a systematic benchmark evaluating whether semantic edits preserve other image content. Experiments on SEAM-Bench and existing benchmark PIE-Bench demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach for controlled image editing. Our results show how a model's own possible outcomes can inform reliable and controllable generation.

papers.title: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk
papers.abstract: We study risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in finite discounted infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes with recursive entropic risk measures (ERM), parameterized by $β\neq 0$. We consider both risk-averse ($β>0$) and risk-seeking ($β<0$) settings. We consider the offline RL setting, where the agent is provided with a fixed dataset and wishes to learn a near-optimal policy using this dataset. We introduce a model-based algorithm, called ERM Value Iteration Lower Confidence Bound (ERM-VI-LCB) and derive a PAC-type bound on its sample complexity. We also establish a corresponding lower bound, demonstrating that exponential dependence on $|β|/(1-γ)$ asserted by the upper bound is unavoidable in the worst case. The presented bounds provide the first rigorous sample complexity guarantees for offline RL under recursive ERM across both risk-averse and risk-seeking regimes.

papers.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases. The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources. By randomizing over candidate edits, we express the loss change of an edit as a derivative with respect to the probability of selecting it, and we evaluate joint edits as single candidates because their changes interact. Schema Descent instantiates the method for graph schemas. In experiments on large documents, each a bundle of research papers, the updated knowledge cards and graph schemas obtain higher mean Answer F1 on held-out generated questions than their initial structures, with schema gains in every document. On human questions, mean F1 rises for schemas and falls for cards: the updated structures serve the kind of question they were learned from.

papers.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
papers.abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.

papers.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality. Whether their outputs still carry model-specific characteristics matters for attribution, for model comparison beyond aggregate quality, and for evaluations that assume anonymity. We ask whether images from frontier T2I models can still be classified by source, and which visual properties make this possible. Here we show that a standard ResNet-50 identifies the source of an image among HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, the four highest-ranked open-source models on the Text-to-Image Arena, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts. Human participants reach only 62.61% on the pairwise version of this task, so the distinguishing cues are not visually obvious. They are also not tied to a particular classifier and survive severe image corruptions and out-of-distribution prompts. We trace them to visual idiosyncrasies at three levels. Low-level texture statistics alone let a lightweight multi-layer perceptron match ResNet-50. Object layout, depth, and albedo estimated from the images each carry a source signal. Image captions reveal model-specific preferences in style and background that the prompts never specify. A one-sentence hint about these cues raises human accuracy by 9.03 percentage points. These idiosyncrasies make source classification a tool for measuring similarity between models and between real and generated images, and they caution against assuming anonymity in human preference evaluation of T2I models.

papers.title: Quot schemes on projective space
papers.abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.

papers.title: Sharp constant in 2D critical fermionic Hardy inequality
papers.abstract: We study the large-$N$ behavior of the optimal constant $κ_N$ in the two-dimensional fermionic many-particle Hardy inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^N -Δ_i \geq κ_N^{(2)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^2}, \] understood as a quadratic-form inequality on antisymmetric wave functions. We prove that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)κ_N^{(2)}=4, \] thereby proving a conjecture of Frank, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Solovej. The proof combines a dyadic Fefferman-de la Llave representation of the Coulomb kernel with separate estimates for squares of low and high particle occupation. A trace inequality controls the low-occupation regime, while sums of Neumann eigenvalues yield the sharp bound in the high-occupation regime.

papers.title: Miyazawa invariants of satellite surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove formulas describing the behavior of Miyazawa's degree invariant of knotted spheres and real projective planes in the 4-sphere under satellite operations. As an application, we show that every deform-spun real projective plane admits infinitely many topologically but not smoothly isotopic copies. In particular, we produce an infinite exotic family of irreducible real projective planes containing Hughes-Kim-Miller-Nahm's counterexample to the Kinoshita conjecture.

papers.title: Measuring a buried Bi$_2$Te$_3$ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
papers.abstract: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--Pérot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi$_2$Te$_3$ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

papers.title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels at https://github.com/tingrui-huang/timestamps-matter.

papers.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
papers.abstract: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to $N \times M$ integrations when evaluating $N$ methods on $M$ benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.

papers.title: Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters
papers.abstract: In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.

papers.title: On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks
papers.abstract: We study Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Szép products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Szép factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Szép actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.

papers.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
papers.abstract: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related knowledge chains, with their geometric mean giving overall coverage. The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. Evaluating 16 deep research agents reveals different strengths in breadth and depth, with the best-performing agent reaching 57.04% overall coverage. Rubric judgments agree closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across the tested metric configurations.

papers.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
papers.abstract: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional Rényi generalizations, defined as differences of Rényi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched Rényi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries under the inversion of the Rényi index, $α\leftrightarrow 1/α$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched Rényi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional Rényi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the Rényi index. Our findings establish a connection between conventional Rényi asymmetries and quantum resource theory, explaining their effectiveness in broad classes of nonequilibrium protocols while highlighting the additional information provided by genuine asymmetry monotones.

papers.title: TIDE-Flow: Fine-Grained Temporal Evidence and Structured Displacement Matching for Spike Optical Flow
papers.abstract: Spike cameras capture high-speed motion through an integrate-and-fire mechanism, providing fine-grained temporal observations without exposure blur. However, their binary streams encode accumulated illumination rather than instantaneous intensity, making reliable motion estimation challenging. Existing spike-based methods exploit temporal aggregation to construct motion representations, but this process may weaken fine-grained firing patterns. Meanwhile, correlation-based estimators often rely on learned matching features without explicitly characterizing the spatial distribution and ambiguity of candidate displacements. To address these challenges, we propose TIDE-Flow, a spike-based optical flow estimation framework that jointly exploits Temporal Integration Evidence (TIE) and Displacement Evidence Encoding (DEE). TIE combines raw spike patterns, multi-scale firing statistics, temporal moments, and boundary-aware interval cues, preserving complementary temporal information before spatial feature compression. DEE further integrates structured candidate-grid features with explicit displacement statistics to characterize matching geometry and competing correspondences. Both components are incorporated into a difference-correlation recurrent refinement framework, enabling effective temporal motion modeling and correspondence estimation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of TIDE-Flow, with controlled ablations validating the contributions of temporal and displacement evidence modeling.

papers.title: Real equiangular lines in dimensions 18-20 and sharp fixed-angle bounds
papers.abstract: In collaboration with OpenAI's GPT-6, we prove that the maximum numbers of real equiangular lines in dimensions 18, 19, and 20 are $N(18)=57$, $N(19)=72$, and $N(20)=90$, respectively. We reduce the upper bounds to paired lattice points in sections of even unimodular lattices of rank twenty-four. Root-system estimates, exact certificates, and Golay-code arguments bound the sections. In the Leech lattice, generalized Hamming weights of a binary evaluation code give sharp bounds attained by nested sections. At prescribed cosine $1/q$, we also show that $N_{1/q}(d)=d+7$ for explicit intervals of consecutive dimensions for each odd $q\ge319$, and $N_{1/q}(d)=d+23$ on such intervals for each odd $q\ge5599$. Regular graphs in repeated Seidel blocks vary the cosine while preserving nullity, and a coherence bound proves optimality. Symmetric conference matrices give a further sharp family at quadratic irrational cosines.

papers.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
papers.abstract: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\toμ^+μ^-$ and $K_L\toπ^0ν\barν$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.

papers.title: An offset--drift Kalman filter for continuous emotion recognition and annotation from sparse human reviews
papers.abstract: Continuous emotion recognition tracks how emotion changes over time, but its predictions often deviate from human ratings, and the traces it is trained on are rated in real time by several annotators, which is slow and costly. A few human reviews could help with both, but rejection only decides which predictions to hand over and adaptation adjusts the model or its outputs; neither uses reviews to correct unreviewed windows directly. We propose a Kalman-filter correction that models the predictor's error as a per-part offset plus a slow drift, estimates it from the reviewed windows and corrects every unreviewed window online, leaving the predictor unchanged. On MSP-Conversation, it beats four simpler corrections in all 48 paired comparisons, keeps correcting each part after reviewing stops and, for uncorrected predictions, tells a person which windows to take over. The same correction serves annotation: with 20% of windows reviewed, the completed trace comes closer to the raters.

papers.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
papers.abstract: Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix. We ask whether fine-tuning the model to the decision objective can do better. We fine-tune the same pretrained model so that its restricted softmax over label tokens (already a distribution over business actions) maximizes expected utility under an institution-specified, amount-scaled cost matrix. Because the reward is a known function of (action, outcome, amount) and the outcome is observed in the data, the expected-utility objective and its gradient are available in closed form. This is example-dependent cost-sensitive learning whose per-example loss is linear in the predicted probability, with no sampling, critics, or advantage estimation. A KL anchor to the pretrained model and an auxiliary language-modeling term preserve calibration and the generative event model. A sampled, group-normalized (GRPO-style) variant provides the extension point to trajectory-level rewards.

papers.title: Model Weights, Airlocks and Sandboxes: A Call for Technical Validation of Re-identification Tests under the EDPB Anonymisation Guidelines
papers.abstract: The Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), published for consultation in July 2026, assess anonymity relative to the entities that may access data. They bring AI models into scope and call for testing, but do not say how a re-identification test should be designed or validated, or how far its result counts as evidence. Building on our reply to the consultation, we describe a framework based on a secure processing environment whose outputs are reviewed before release (an airlock), and distinguish forms of release and three types of evidence: formal, empirical and indirect. We raise seven open questions, each with a scenario, and examine their technical side in three settings: the release of model weights (the trained parameters of a machine learning model), review at an airlock, and regulatory sandboxes, in which an authority supervises development and testing. In each setting the assessment depends on how far a test result can be relied on, since a failed re-identification attempt may mean only that the test was too weak. Drawing on measurement practice in other regulated fields, we call for re-identification tests to be validated as measurement methods, with stated detection limit, bias and uncertainty.

papers.title: DocDUR-Net: Degradation-Aware Unified Document Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Captured document images often suffer from diverse degradations caused by uncontrolled imaging conditions, which reduce readability and obscure fine text structures. Single-degradation restoration methods are usually trained and deployed for individual degradation types, and therefore require model selection before restoration. Unified restoration models alleviate the need to maintain multiple restoration networks by sharing one network across tasks, but representative unified document image restoration methods still depend on external task selection. This dependency limits automatic document image restoration. We propose DocDUR-Net, a degradation-aware unified restoration network that derives restoration guidance directly from the input image. It introduces a Degradation Perception Module (DPM) to extract degradation representations and predict degradation weights, and Degradation Prior-guided Adaptive Feature Fusion (DP-AFF) to combine learnable degradation priors with degradation features extracted from the input. The resulting guidance is injected into a shared restoration backbone, enabling adaptive restoration without external task selection. DocDUR-Net also supports a manual mode with explicit task selection. Experiments on document image restoration benchmarks show that DocDUR-Net achieves the best average PSNR of 29.405 dB and SSIM of 0.960 among unified methods while remaining competitive with single-degradation methods.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Equilibrium Learning in Symmetric Congestion Games under Semi-Bandit Feedback
papers.abstract: We study last-iterate learning of mixed Nash equilibria in atomic symmetric congestion games under resource semi-bandit feedback, where players observe both the costs and the loads of their selected resources. For strictly increasing latency functions, the restriction of the potential function to symmetric marginal profiles is strongly convex. However, players' independent stochastic updates need not preserve this symmetry without explicit synchronization. We show that a quadratic consensus penalty makes the potential globally strongly convex while making the symmetric equilibrium the unique minimizer of the transformed potential. We propose a variant of online projected gradient descent that achieves $O(t^{-2/3})$ squared distance to equilibrium and $O(t^{-1/3})$ maximum deviation gain in expectation, for every $t\geq 1$ and for any initialization. The played profile also converges to equilibrium almost surely.

papers.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
papers.abstract: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets. We pair images from these datasets with VLM-generated and human-verified referring expressions, and derive accurate ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes of the referred objects from their 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Our systematic evaluation of 17 frontier VLMs across the major proprietary and open-weight families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen, Gemma) shows that the best model, Gemini 4 Carbon, reaches 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D, despite the more lenient IoU thresholds in 3D. The predicted 3D boxes are usually centered on the target objects in the image but often off in depth by more than the object's size, suggesting that metric scale estimation, which needs reliable object size priors, is currently by far the main source of error.

papers.title: Focus Only on What's Important: Training-Free Focus Maps for Frozen Vision Transformers in Long-Video Object Segmentation
papers.abstract: Vision transformers are strong but costly image encoders for video object segmentation. Training-free token merging cuts compute uniformly across the frame, including on tracked objects. We give a frozen DINOv3 ViT inside a trained Cutie head a training-free focus map: full resolution where the segmenter expects its objects and coarser merging elsewhere. Protecting only the previous frame's mask works on short clips but fails on long videos, where fast motion pushes targets outside the margin and into background merging, locking in loss. Our policy instead takes the union of velocity-shifted and block-matched masks, runs a camera-compensated surprise check, delegates uncertain regions to the compared merger, and falls back to it when all objects are lost. On long videos (LVOS V2 valid, pre-specified protocol, three ViT-S seeds), it beats ALGM 0.98 by +2.76 J&F (95% object CI [+1.22,+4.44]; video-cluster [+0.99,+4.52]) at 16% fewer counted encoder FLOPs (0.385 vs. 0.459), sitting 1.0 J&F point below the dense-encoder baseline; at ViT-B the gain over ALGM 0.95 is +3.89 [+2.03,+5.87]. On DAVIS 2017 val it stays within -0.19 J&F of the dense encoder at ViT-S (-0.12 at ViT-B). Controls qualify the result: protecting only the previous mask under ALGM matches or exceeds accuracy at higher FLOPs (0.486), so expectation and surprise mainly reduce counted encoder compute. Practically, lower counted encoder compute did not reduce startup-inclusive mean Cutie step time on a 12-video LVOS sample (3%-8% lower in steady state; an equally engineered ALGM is faster at ViT-S and ViT-B). Section 5.2 separately examines a Cutie permanent-memory schedule and its latency and memory trade-offs. Code: https://github.com/boletoms/focused-cv

papers.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Since vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, accelerating these demonstrations before fine-tuning can lead to faster VLA policies without an additional speed-selection module at deployment. Several offline speedup methods have focused on identifying segments that require less precision and assigning predefined speedup factors to the segments. However, even within a single segment, a speedup factor suitable for steady motion may be too high when precise alignment is required. To this end, this paper presents RePace, an offline reasoning framework that determines how much to accelerate each part of a demonstration. For the same recorded movement, RePace measures how much each candidate speedup factor shortens the sequence and compares the resulting observation-action pairs used for training. Given the task instruction, a pretrained language model uses the visual context and original motion of successive windows to interpret these candidate retiming effects and select a speedup profile for the complete episode. Experimental results demonstrate that RePace outperforms the baselines in overall task execution efficiency on both LIBERO and RoboCasa-Kitchen. On all three tasks with a gripper-equipped Franka Research 3 arm, RePace matches or exceeds the acceleration baselines in success rate and completes successful trials faster.

papers.title: State convertibility in quantum-state texture from a general form of free operations
papers.abstract: State convertibility specifies which transformations between states a quantum resource theory allows. In quantum-state texture, deterministic conversion criteria are known for qubits and pure sources in arbitrary dimension, but a general criterion for mixed states in higher dimensions is missing. We derive this exact criterion from a complete characterization of free operations in arbitrary finite dimension. Because the unique free state is pure, every free operation splits into a quantum filter and a residual completely positive map. Using this decomposition, we show that every allowed conversion admits a two-outcome measurement that retains the filtered state after one outcome and prepares a fixed state after the other. Conversion thus reduces to finding such a filter whose unnormalized output leaves a positive semidefinite remainder when subtracted from the target, a search we show to be solvable by semidefinite programming. Beyond deterministic conversion, the characterization of free operations can be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. More broadly, since the construction relies on a pure fixed state, it also applies to other resource theories defined by free operations fixing such a state.

papers.title: Adaptive Control Barrier Functions for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems
papers.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have emerged as a flexible and efficient approach for enforcing dynamic safety constraints. In this paper, we consider a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with singular perturbations and develop an adaptive CBF framework for such systems to enforce safety constraints on both the slow and fast subsystems in the overall singularly perturbed nonlinear system with uncertain parameters. We first develop a robustness property showing that if an adaptive controller for the slow subsystem satisfies the slow CBF condition with an appropriate safety margin, then for sufficiently small values of the singular perturbation parameter $\varepsilon$, the slow subsystem remains within an $O(\varepsilon)$-neighborhood of its safe set. We then consider the more general case of safety constraints on both the fast and slow subsystems and provide conditions under which joint slow-fast safety is achieved despite the parametric uncertainties. The reduced-order slow model and the slow and fast CBF conditions are evaluated using an online parameter estimate and the parameter mismatch between the estimated and true reduced-order models is addressed via a state-dependent robustness margin in the CBF inequalities. To illustrate the proposed framework, we present simulation studies for two systems with parametric uncertainties: a synthetic two-time-scale fourth-order example system and a unicycle with a fast turn-rate actuator and an obstacle avoidance safety constraint.

papers.title: The oxygen cold trap in protoplanetary discs
papers.abstract: The diffusive transport of oxygen in protoplanetary discs followed by sequestration into ice in the midplane, a process known as the cold trap, can substantially alter the chemical environment where planets form. This paper presents a new time-dependent modelling framework that allows us to consistently simulate kinetic gas-phase chemistry, ice growth and desorption, turbulent diffusive mixing, and gravitational settling of icy particles with a changing particle size distribution over million-year timescales in one-dimensional vertical columns. Applying our model to a T Tauri disc across radii from 1 to 100 au reveals that vertical cold trapping becomes an effective mechanism once the diffusion-to-settling timescale ratio exceeds unity, simultaneously driving the gas-phase C/O up toward unity, and the gas-phase C/H down, by up to two orders of magnitude at large distances. All models feature the development of an upward counter-flux due to the turbulent up-whirling of icy particles followed by ice sublimation above the horizontal icelines, which brings the cold trapping to a halt and eventually establishes a relaxed vertical structure after about $10^4$ to $10^6$ yr, depending on the radial distance. The ice formation leads to a strongly peaked size distribution around 1 mic, which contains the majority of the condensed mass in the disc after ice formation, and changes the dynamical behaviour of the grains substantially. We conclude that the vertical cold trap can provide an important part of the explanation why evolved discs observed with ALMA often show high C/O ratios as inferred from strong emissions from hydrocarbon molecules in the outer disc, such as C2H and c-C3H2. However, in none of our models does the C/O ratio exceed unity, which is a consequence of CO-blocking, a chemical process where water molecules naturally stop forming once C/O approaches unity.

papers.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.

papers.title: Pinwheel Scheduling is PSPACE-Complete
papers.abstract: Pinwheel Scheduling is a classical periodic scheduling problem, receiving as input the deadlines $d_i$ of $n$ tasks and asking for an infinite schedule with one task per time unit, such that every task $i$ is scheduled at least once in every $d_i$ time units. Holte, Mok, Rosier, Tulchinsky, and Varvel introduced the problem in 1989 and showed that it lies in \(\PSPACE\). Its exact complexity has been open since then. \(\NP\)-hardness for explicitly listed deadlines was established only recently, and membership in \(\NP\) is open. In this work we prove that Pinwheel Scheduling is \(\PSPACE\)-complete when the deadlines are written in binary. This finally settles the long-standing open question about the complexity of Pinwheel Scheduling. We present a chain of reductions, starting from Periodic 3-SAT, a classical \(\PSPACE\)-complete problem, and using two newly-defined intermediate periodic scheduling problems. These intermediate problems can be seen as periodically assigning tasks to days, with each day containing a fixed number of slots (\emph{hours}) in which tasks are scheduled. In the first of these problems, each day is additionally allowed to contain \emph{breaks}, that is, hours in which no task can be scheduled.

papers.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
papers.abstract: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones. We describe and evaluate a three-way merge in which the schema defines a conflict: set algebra combines canonical triples, and a slot is contended only where a SHACL shape bounds its cardinality and both sides' changes cannot stand within that bound. Unbounded predicates union; contended slots go to a person. The same shapes graph validates the result. We do not claim the first three-way merge for RDF. Our contribution is an implementation in a production multi-agent store and an evaluation against a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge overlap rule, which it extends rather than replaces, and six other strategies. Across five synthetic seeds, the shape-aware operator raised 33 conflicts, all true positives as judged by the same shapes that define them, with no triples lost or fabricated and no SHACL violations admitted. The context-overlap baseline, counted per slot, detected the same 33 conflicts but asked 845 questions.
